title: Winning for Kent: procurement with purpose
post: Kent County Council spends about £1.47 billion each year on goods, services, and works. Its 2026–28 Procurement with Purpose Policy sets out how that purchasing power should also support skills and jobs, local organisations, and healthier communities.

title: Reimagining commissioning: relational and learning-centred approaches
post: What would commissioning look like if relationships and learning were treated as infrastructure rather than soft additions? Dan Kirby and Steph Gamauf set out a direction shaped by trust, shared purpose, continuous feedback, and adaptation.

title: Earlier relational support for people with dementia: the Live More evaluation
post: Live More matched people living with dementia with Shared Lives carers before crisis. Its evaluation reports stronger wellbeing and independence, trusted respite for families, earlier identification of problems, and an estimated £5.96 of social value for each £1 invested.

title: Air-quality innovation masterclass — 14 October 2026
post: Online, 14 October, 10:00–11:30 UK time: Westminster and the Innovation Procurement Empowerment Centre share what they learned from defining an air-quality challenge, engaging innovative suppliers, running a live trial, and building evidence for future decisions.

title: A practical collection of relational services resources
post: Where can you start with relational services? Q Community has assembled an unusually useful collection of reports, practical guides, recordings, organisations, and communities working beyond siloed and transactional services.

title: A season for change? The Relationships Project on relational reform
post: Can a state built around standardisation, targets, and control become more relational? Rich Bell at the Relationships Project looks at devolution, public-service reform, and social care as practical tests of whether trust, connection, and agency can shape how government works.

title: The Mayor’s Bear: stories of hope and local democracy
post: Local democracy is usually explained in institutional language. Jon Harvey takes another route: stories for children about playgrounds, refugees, dementia-friendly towns, and the possibility of changing one part of the world around you. Jon is a regular PSTA facilitator.

title: The neighbourhood that had no plan: a story by Mike Chitty
post: What happens when residents are invited into a programme after the outcomes have already been decided? Mike Chitty's short story makes a familiar neighbourhood-working problem concrete: the neighbourhood is asked to fit the plan, rather than the plan learning from the neighbourhood.

title: Rewiring the state: the LGIU on local government's role
post: If more responsibility moves locally, capability has to move with it. LGIU's 'Rewiring the state' is useful on prevention, democratic accountability, finance, and what councils need if reform is to change more than structures.

title: Associations and institutions: Cormac Russell on how change happens
post: Institutions can provide services consistently at scale. Associations can mobilise relationships, mutual care, and contribution. Cormac Russell's distinction matters because public services can crowd out what people do together while trying to help.

title: Reading: Mike Barker on prevention and the role of councils
post: A cut can be a saving in one budget and a cost somewhere else, later. Mike Barker asks what happens when councils protect urgent statutory services while the places and relationships that help people stay well are allowed to erode.

title: A commissioning instincts quiz from Ideas Alliance
post: Commissioning choices reveal what we reach for first: governance, performance, partnership, or adaptation to complex needs. The Ideas Alliance five-question quiz is useful as a team conversation starter — not as a capability test.

title: The debrief is where a simulation becomes learning
post: A simulation gives people shared experience. A careful debrief connects that experience with the decisions they face at work.

title: Make the contract review useful to both sides
post: What has changed for people using the service, and what decision follows? Five questions for a more useful contract review.

title: Give a learning programme a real piece of work
post: Choose a bounded piece of work, a sponsor who can act, and a way to review what changes. Making a development programme useful in practice.

title: Find the decision your partnership cannot currently make
post: Which shared decision keeps coming back without resolution? Use it to examine authority, evidence, and relationships across a partnership.

title: Commissioning starts with a question about purpose
post: Before writing the specification, ask what someone should be able to do, experience, or achieve. A PSTA practice note on commissioning and purpose.

title: Choose a development route around the work ahead
post: An individual learner, an organisational team, and a partnership need different kinds of development. Start by identifying who must learn and act together.

title: The National Commissioning Academy returns in November 2026
post: The National Commissioning Academy returns in November 2026. The next cohort combines anchor days, expert sessions, action learning, a national peer network, and a practical 100-day plan. Places are £2,490 excluding VAT, with discounts for group bookings and host organisations.
